# Standalone sandbox, part 2: `--sandbox` runs, resume, open, list and clean ## What to build Make `graph-execution --spec s --provider p --sandbox` run the whole run inside a Docker container started with the local `docker` CLI, with no graph-manager. It reuses what already exists: - `src/sandbox/docker.ts`: the docker CLI wrapper (`dockerAvailable`, `imageExists`, `build`, `imagePath`, `create`, `cp`, `start`, `inspect`, `port`, `logs`, `rm`); - `src/sandbox/image.ts` (`resolveImage`); - `src/sandbox/engine.ts` (`ensureEngineCopy`); - `src/sandbox/settings.ts` (`resolveSandboxSettings` with the `--sandbox-image/--sandbox-base/--sandbox-line/--no-sandbox-config-lines/--sandbox-cpus/--sandbox-memory/--sandbox-pids` flags); - the config `sandbox` section; - in the web server: `?token=` + the `ge_token` cookie, and `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_PUBLIC_PORT` (`WEB_PUBLIC_PORT_ENV`). Read those files first. **This task declares the run flags on the root command** (`--sandbox-image `, `--sandbox-base `, `--sandbox-line ` repeatable with the `collect` helper, `--no-sandbox-config-lines`, `--sandbox-cpus `, `--sandbox-memory `, `--sandbox-pids `) and passes them to `resolveSandboxSettings`; the `sandbox build|dockerfile|config` subcommands already have their own `--image/--base/--line`. Add every new valued flag to `RUN_VALUE_OPTIONS` in `src/state/paths.ts`; `cli.test.ts` L62-77 checks that the list matches `--help`. ### Starting a sandboxed run (host side), in `src/sandbox/run.ts` `startSandboxedRun(opts)` 1. **Refusals** (`UsageError`, exit 2, checked before anything is created): - `process.platform === "win32"`: `the sandbox needs Linux or macOS; on Windows use WSL` - `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX=1`: `already running in a sandbox` - no docker, or no daemon: `--sandbox needs Docker: the docker command was not found or cannot reach a daemon` - the `suite` command with `--sandbox`: `suites cannot run in a sandbox yet` Note: **inside a graph-manager terminal**, graph-manager's own `graph-execution` shim intercepts `--sandbox` first, so the engine never sees it there. Keep that working. 2. **Preflight** on the host as for `--web` (`preflight({...})` in `src/launch/preflight.ts`). This validates tasks, spec, reviewers, config and provider names. The provider CLIs need not be on the host: pass a `skipProviderCheck` option (new) to preflight for a sandboxed start. The image check below replaces it. 3. **Run id and dir.** Generate the run id (`generateRunId` in `src/runner/startup.ts` ~L79). The run dir is `runsRoot(repo)/`; create it. 4. **Image.** `resolveSandboxSettings` + `resolveImage` with the providers = run provider ∪ review provider ∪ reviewers' providers. - For a build, run `build` only when `imageExists(tag)` is false, streaming to stdout. - For a ready-made image, check each provider bin with `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh -c 'command -v '`. Exit 2 `image has no on its PATH` when one is missing. - Then `imagePath(image)`. 5. **Engine.** `ensureEngineCopy()` → mounted read-only at `/opt/graph-execution`. 6. **Container**, named `ge-sbx-`, created with `docker create` and these flags: - `--init` - `--hostname sbx-<8 hex>` - `--user :` (from `fs.stat(repo top level)`) - `--security-opt no-new-privileges` - `--cpus`, `--memory m`, `--pids-limit` - `-v :` (rw; `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) - `-v :/opt/graph-execution:ro` - `-w ` - `-p 127.0.0.1::7600`, where `hostPort` is a free port found by listening on port 0 and closing - `--label graph-execution.run=` - env with `-e K=V`: - the provider login keys (`loginEnvKeys()` from the catalog) that are set on the host - `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` and `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL` from the env, else from `git config user.name` / `user.email` in the repo - `TZ`, `LANG` - the names in `sandbox.env` - every host `GRAPH_EXECUTION_*` var except the internal ones (`RUN_ENV_UNSET` in paths.ts, plus `GRAPH_EXECUTION_HANDOFF`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX*`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_*`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_DELEGATE*`) - then `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX=1`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX_IMAGE=`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID=`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_PORT=7600`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_PUBLIC_PORT=`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_TOKEN=`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE=/.ready.json` (**required by `--web-serve`**, cli.ts ~L278), `HOME=/home/sandbox`, `PATH=` (Docker does not expand `$PATH` in env) - on resume, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM=` - command: `node /opt/graph-execution/dist/cli.js --web-serve`. Keep `--review-provider` etc. 7. **Login copy.** Stage the login files of every provider in the run (`providerInfo(p).loginFiles`, relative to HOME; a trailing `/` is a folder) into a fresh `mkdtemp` dir with mode 0700 (files 0600). Run `docker cp -a /. ge-sbx-:/home/sandbox`, then `rm -rf` the temp dir, also on failure. A non-fake provider with no login file and none of its `loginEnv` set → exit 2 `no

login to copy into the sandbox: log in once, or set `. This mirrors graph-manager's `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts` `loginEntries` (L87-128). 8. **Start** and wait up to 60 s for `/.ready.json` (poll every 200 ms; fail early when `inspect` says the container exited). - Write `/sandbox.json` `{ container, image, hostname, url: "http://127.0.0.1:/", token, host: os.hostname() }` with mode 0600. - Print `Run started in a sandbox: http://127.0.0.1:/?token=`. - Open it with `openInBrowser` (src/readme/readme.ts L40-44), skipped over SSH like `launchWeb` does (src/launch/launch.ts ~L111-120). Exit 0. - On failure: print `docker logs`, `docker rm -f` the container, exit 2. `--sandbox` implies `--web`; passing `--web` as well is fine. ### State and liveness - `state.json` `sandbox`: today `z.object({ image: z.string() })` (src/state/state.ts L89), recorded in run.ts ~L193 from `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX_IMAGE`. Extend it to `{ image, base?, lines?, cpus?, memoryMb?, pids? }`, passed in as a JSON env var `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX_SETTINGS` (add it to `RUN_ENV_UNSET`), so `--resume --sandbox` reuses the same settings. The image flags are refused with `--resume`, like `--reviewers` (preflight.ts ~L242). - **Foreign locks.** `lockHolder` (state.ts L281-286) treats a lock from another host as held forever. When `/sandbox.json` exists, use `docker inspect` of its container instead: - running → live - exited or missing → not live - docker unavailable → treated as live, i.e. unknown Wire this into: - `src/cleanup/scan.ts` `readRun` (L75-98): `kind`, and `pid` replaced by a `container` field for display - `src/cleanup/list.ts`: show `(sandbox ge-sbx-…)` instead of `(pid N)` - `src/launch/open.ts` `openRun` (L44-68): for a sandboxed run, use `sandbox.json`'s `url?token=` when the container runs; otherwise "has no live page" - `src/cleanup/clean.ts` / `execute.ts`: remove the exited `ge-sbx-` container of a run it deletes - `assertNotRunning` (preflight.ts L294-301) Keep the liveness lookup in one helper, `sandboxLiveness(runDir)` in `src/sandbox/run.ts`, with an injectable docker for tests. - `acquireLock`'s foreign-lock message (state.ts ~L316) becomes `run is locked by process on host (a sandbox); resume it with graph-execution --resume --run --sandbox, or from graph-manager`. - **Resume.** `--resume --run --sandbox`: - If `inspect` says the old container is running, exit 2 `the run's sandbox is still running`. - Otherwise `docker rm` the old container, read the old hostname from `sandbox.json`, and start a new container as above, with args `--resume --run `, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM=`, the saved settings, and a new token and port. Then rewrite `sandbox.json`. - A plain `--resume` of a sandboxed run keeps exiting 2. Update its message (preflight.ts L260-264) to `run ran in a sandbox: resume it with graph-execution --resume --run --sandbox, or from graph-manager`. **Also update the test asserting the old text** (cli.test.ts ~L645). - **cli.ts.** Replace the refusal `if (opts.sandbox) throw new UsageError("--sandbox needs graph-manager");` (~L254) with the call to `startSandboxedRun`. Update the help text to `run in a Docker sandbox (see README "Sandbox")`. Update cli.test.ts ~L598-604, which expects the old refusal: with `onlyNodeAndGit` it must now expect `--sandbox needs Docker`. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `src/cli.ts`: - `RunOptions` (L31-57) - the action (~L253-307) with the `--web` branch (`launchWeb`) and `--web-serve` (needs `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE`) - `serveWeb` (L180-203) - `suite` (L357-415) - `src/launch/launch.ts` (the `launchWeb` flow and its injectable deps), `src/launch/open.ts`, `src/readme/readme.ts` `openInBrowser`. - `src/web/serve.ts`: `announceReady` writes `{url, runId, pid}` to the ready file; web.json inside the container has the container's hostname and port 7600, so the host must use `sandbox.json`. - `src/state/state.ts`: L65-90, L180-188 `isAlive`, L194 `lockHost`, L211-225 `parseLock`, L236-248, L281-337. - `src/state/paths.ts` (all constants). - `src/cleanup/scan.ts`, `list.ts`, `clean.ts`, `execute.ts`, `plan.ts` (L52, L56: live runs skipped with `running (pid N)`). - graph-manager's flow to mirror: `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` L556-649 (start), `sandbox-run.ts` L153-189 (`sandboxEnv`) and L192-209 (`gitIdentity`), `routes/resume.ts` L49-60 (the takeLockFrom logic). ## Tests (fake docker) Write a fake `docker` (with `writeFakeBin` from `src/__fixtures__/fake-bin.ts`) in `src/__fixtures__/fake-docker.ts`, a Node script that: - appends each argv and stdin to `$FAKE_DOCKER_LOG` (JSONL); - keeps container state in `$FAKE_DOCKER_STATE` (JSON); - answers `version`, `image inspect` (exists per state), `build`, `create`, `cp` (records the source dir listing **and copies the files into `$FAKE_DOCKER_STATE.d//home`**, so a test can check the login files arrived), `start`, `inspect` (`{"State":{"Running":true}}` per state), `port`, `logs` and `rm`. - **Exec mode** (`FAKE_DOCKER_EXEC=1`): `start` actually runs the container's command locally as a detached child, with the `-e` env applied, `HOME` mapped to the state home dir, and `/opt/graph-execution` mapped to the engine copy path. The real run then happens with `--provider fake`, and the ready file and web page appear. Tests in `src/sandbox/run.test.ts`, plus CLI tests in `src/cli.test.ts`: - [ ] No docker (`onlyNodeAndGit`) → exit 2 `--sandbox needs Docker`, and no `.graph-execution`. - [ ] `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX=1` + `--sandbox` → exit 2 `already running in a sandbox`. - [ ] Not exec mode: the docker log shows `build` (or none when the tag exists), then `create` with `-v :`, `--user`, `--init`, `-p 127.0.0.1::7600`, env `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_PUBLIC_PORT`, and no `GM_` vars; then `cp -a`, then `start`. The staged temp dir no longer exists. The test writes the ready file itself to let the start finish. `sandbox.json` is written, stdout has `?token=`, exit 0. - [ ] Exec mode, end to end with the diamond fixture and `--provider fake`: the run reaches `applied`; `graph-execution list` shows it; `graph-execution open` (with an injected opener, or `SSH_CONNECTION=1` to print instead) gives the `?token=` URL while running; after the container is marked exited, `list` no longer shows it live. - [ ] `--resume --run --sandbox` with the old container running → exit 2 `the run's sandbox is still running`. With it gone → a new `create` with `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM=sbx-…`. - [ ] `--sandbox-image my/img --sandbox-line x` → exit 2. `--sandbox-base node:22-bookworm --sandbox-line 'RUN echo hi'` → the build's Dockerfile starts `FROM node:22-bookworm` and has the line, and state.json `sandbox.base`/`lines` record them. - [ ] `suite … --sandbox` → exit 2 `suites cannot run in a sandbox yet`. Skip the docker-dependent tests on Windows (`describe.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`), and assert the Windows refusal with an injected platform. ## README Fill in the "Sandbox (Docker)" section (after "Safety"), and update "Safety" (~L575-577) and the Quick-start callout (L33) to point to `--sandbox`. Cover: - the flow; - what is mounted (only the repo; the engine read-only); - the login copy (a macOS Keychain login is not a file: use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`); - the URL with token; - `open`, `list`, `clean` and resume; - the limits, which are not on Windows (WSL), not for suites, and include no network filtering. Add the `--sandbox*` flags to the usage line (L86) and flags table (L97-122). ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-execution -- src/sandbox src/cli.test.ts src/cleanup src/launch src/state ```
